results.name: Eagle Arms Chin Into Chest
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides. Raise both arms outward to shoulder height, then bring them forward in front of your chest.
Cross one upper arm over the other at the elbows, bend both elbows, and wrap your forearms around each other until the back of your hands press together.
Lift your elbows in front of your face, gently tuck your chin toward your chest, and allow your upper back to round slightly until you feel a stretch across your shoulders, upper back, and neck.
Hold the position briefly, then lift your head, unwrap your arms, and return them to your sides. Repeat with the opposite arm crossed on top.
tips: Wrap your forearms only as far as your shoulder mobility comfortably allows.
Press the backs of your arms together if your hands cannot meet.
Keep your elbows lifted while gently drawing your shoulder blades apart.
Inhale as you prepare and exhale as you tuck your chin and deepen the stretch.
results.description: Eagle Arms Chin Into Chest is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Neck, Middle Back.

results.name: Easy Pose Neck Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart, your shoulders relaxed, and your arms resting by your sides.
Raise one arm over your head and place your hand gently above the opposite ear
Slowly draw your head toward the raised-arm side, bringing your ear toward your shoulder while keeping your opposite shoulder lowered and your torso upright.
Hold the stretch, then release your head gradually and lower your arm before repeating on the opposite side.
tips: Draw your head gently toward your shoulder instead of pulling forcefully.
Keep your spine tall and avoid rounding your upper back.
Stop if you feel pinching, dizziness, or discomfort in your neck.
Inhale before tilting your head and exhale as you relax into the stretch.
results.description: Easy Pose Neck Stretch is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Easy Seated Twist Pose
instructions: Sit upright with your legs crossed, placing your shins parallel to each other. Rest both hands on your leg on top and lengthen your spine.
Rotate your torso to one side, placing the back of your opposite forearm above your knee, and position your other hand on the floor behind your hips for support.
Keep your hips grounded as you rotate your chest and shoulders toward your rear hand, then gently turn your head to look over the same shoulder.
Hold the stretch, return your torso and head to the center with control, then reverse your hand placement and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Position your rear hand close to your body to support an upright posture.
Rotate through your torso without forcing the movement with your arms.
Use the hand on your opposite knee only as a gentle guide.
Inhale as you lengthen your spine and exhale as you rotate deeper into the stretch.
results.description: Easy Seated Twist Pose is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Core, Lower Back, Upper Back.

results.name: Extended Side Angle Pose With Block
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and place a yoga block vertically in front of your right toes. Step your left foot back and out to the side into a wide stance, turning your foot outward. Keep your left leg extended, and bend your right knee.
Lean your torso toward your right thigh and place your right hand on top of the block, using it for light support while keeping both feet firmly planted.
Rotate your chest open, raising your left arm toward the ceiling, then bend your elbow and reach your forearm over your head to lengthen the side of your torso.

Hold the position, then raise your left arm toward the ceiling, lift your torso upright, straighten your right leg, and step your left foot forward. Repeat on the opposite side with the block positioned in front of your left toes.
tips: Place only light pressure through your right hand instead of leaning heavily on the block.
Keep both feet firmly planted and maintain a stable, wide stance.
Keep your right knee aligned with your right toes without allowing it to collapse inward.
Inhale as you rotate your chest open and exhale as you reach your arm over your head.
results.description: Extended Side Angle Pose With Block is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Adductors, Quadriceps, Glutes.

results.name: Extended Side Angle Pose
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart, then step one foot back and out to the side into a wide stance. Turn your back foot outward and keep your back leg extended, while bending the knee of your front leg.
Lean your torso toward your front thigh and place your same-side hand on the floor inside your front foot, keeping both feet firmly planted.
Rotate your chest open, raise your opposite arm toward the ceiling, then bend your elbow and reach your forearm over your head to lengthen the side of your torso.
Hold the position, then straighten your upper arm, lift your torso, straighten your front leg, and step back to the starting position before repeating on the opposite side.
tips: Use your lower hand lightly for balance instead of placing all your weight through it.
Rotate your chest upward and avoid allowing your upper shoulder to roll forward.
Keep your hips stable as you lengthen your upper arm over your head.
Inhale as you open your chest and exhale as you deepen the side stretch.
results.description: Extended Side Angle Pose is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Glutes, Hamstrings.

results.name: Gate Pose Rounding Spine Looking Up
instructions: Begin in a tall kneeling position. Extend your left leg straight out to the side for support and place your right hand on the floor directly under your shoulder.
Keep your right knee under your hip and your extended leg straight as you lean to the side.
Rotate your chest upward and extend your left arm over your head. Turn your head and look up toward ceiling.
Hold the stretch, then lower your left arm and return upright. Repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Press evenly through your right palm for support.
Rotate your chest upward without allowing your hips to roll backward.
Look upward only as far as your neck remains comfortable.
Inhale while upright and exhale as you lean to the side.
results.description: Gate Pose Rounding Spine Looking Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Gate Pose Variation Arm Extended on Side
instructions: Begin in a tall kneeling position, then extend your left leg straight out to the side for support.
Lean to your right and place your right hand on the floor directly under your shoulder, with your arm extended.
Extend your left arm over your head while keeping your chest and gaze facing forward.
Hold the stretch, then return upright and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Keep your chest facing forward without rotating upward.
Keep your supporting knee directly below your hip.
Keep your hips stable as you bend to the side.
Inhale while upright, then exhale as you lean and extend your arm over your head.
results.description: Gate Pose Variation Arm Extended on Side is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the abs (waist). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Half Lotus
instructions: Sit upright on the floor with both legs extended in front of you.
Bend your left knee and place your left ankle above your right knee so your shins are perpendicular to each other.
Support your left foot with your right hand and place your left hand on your left knee.
Gently press your left knee downward while keeping your torso upright, then release and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Place your ankle just above your knee, not directly on the kneecap.
Press the knee of your working leg downward gently without forcing it.
Keep your spine tall and your shoulders relaxed.
Inhale while sitting upright and exhale as you gently press your knee downward.
results.description: Half Lotus is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Adductors.

results.name: Half Monkey Pose
instructions: Begin in a tall kneeling position, then extend one leg forward with your heel on the floor and your toes pointing upward.
Keep your hips stable above your kneeling knee as you straighten your front leg, keeping your heel on the floor.
Lean forward over your straight leg and place both hands on the floor beside your foot.
Hold the stretch. Return to the starting position, then repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Point your front toes upward to deepen the calf and hamstring stretch.
Position your rear knee comfortably beneath your hip.
Use your hands lightly for support without placing excessive weight through them.
Inhale while you are in the upright position and exhale as you lean forward.
results.description: Half Monkey Pose is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Calves, Glutes, Lower Back.

results.name: Happy Baby
instructions: Lie on your back, bend your knees toward your chest, and hold the outside of each foot with your hands.
Open your knees wider than your torso and raise your feet so the soles face upward.
Gently pull your feet downward while keeping your head, shoulders, and lower back on the floor.
Hold the stretch, then release your feet and return to the starting position.
tips: Keep your ankles positioned above your knees.
Draw your knees toward the sides of your torso.
Use a comfortable range without forcing your hips or knees.
Inhale as you prepare and exhale as you deepen the stretch.
results.description: Happy Baby is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the adductors (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Lower Back.
